name: NWS API (api.weather.gov)
provides: Point-to-grid lookup; 7-day 12-hour and hourly forecasts on about a 2.5 km grid; gridded data; alerts; station observations.
access: HTTPS GET, GeoJSON default; 'A User Agent is required'; no key now, 'will be replaced with an API key in the future'
licensing: 'intended to be open data, free to use for any purpose'
refresh: Forecasts updated by forecast offices; cadence not stated on the documentation page.
latency: Observations may be delayed up to 20 minutes (documentation). Forecast issuance lag not stated.
failure_behavior: Rate-limit errors, retry after ~5 s. Outages announced via NCEP admin messages. The API host was robots-blocked to WebFetch; CORS and browser User-Agent handling UNVERIFIED
browser_cors_or_key_issues: A User-Agent header identifying the application is required, and an API key is planned. Browsers may not let page scripts set User-Agent; CORS and browser handling were not verified (the API host was robots-blocked to the research tool). Fetch at build time (for example a scheduled GitHub Action writing a dated CSV with provenance) so browser CORS and keys never reach the page; the test workflow stays offline.
recommendation: Defer (live integrations are deferred). If a heat panel is built (RULE-CTX-07), take a dated build-time snapshot; never call it live from the static demo, because a live forecast does not match the fictional as_of.
verification_note: [cite_context.json checked[27], claim yes] Page says 'A User Agent is required to identify your application', which 'will be replaced with an API key in the future'. The API is 'intended to be open data, free to use for any purpose'. Rate-limited requests 'may be retried after the limit clears (typically within 5 seconds)'. forecastHourly covers 'the next seven days'. 'Observations may be delayed up to 20 minutes'. Known Issues 'Updated 3/24/2026'. CORS is not mentioned. The '~2.5 km grids' claim was not confirmed in this fetch. || [cite_water.json checked[43], claim yes] Confirmed: 'open data, free to use for any purpose'; 'A User Agent is required'; the /points endpoint; 'about 2.5km x 2.5km'; caching the grid; retry 'typically within 5 seconds'; observations 'delayed up to 20 minutes'; gridX/gridY 'may occasionally change'. Small mislabel: the 'Known Issues' section says 'No significant known issues'. The null 24h max/min 'for stations outside the central time zone' is listed under Upstream Issues/Changes as a MADIS ingest bug, and it affects station observations endpoints, not forecasts. || [cite_health.json checked[29], claim partly] These integration claims are supported verbatim: 'intended to be open data, free to use for any purpose'; 'A User Agent is required to identify your application'; it 'will be replaced with an API key in the future'; 'The rate limit is not public information', retry 'typically within 5 seconds'; 'cache-friendly approach'; /points/{lat},{lon} gives forecastHourly and forecastGridData over seven days; gridX/gridY 'and even the office ... may occasionally change'. Not supported: the data_fields entry forecast_thi_hourly cites this page for 'update_frequency: several times daily (NWS forecast)', but the page states no forecast update frequency. The integration entry itself correctly says 'not stated'. The page does not state coverage beyond NWS Weather Forecast Office grids (about 2.5 km).
merged_research_notes: [water integration 0] provides: 7-day 12-hour and hourly forecasts on a 2.5 km grid; station observations; failure: Rate-limit errors (retry after about 5 s). Grid points can change, so re-check /points. Known issue: 24 h max/min null outside Central time. The Great Plains ranch would be in Central or Mountain time. | [health integration 0] provides: 7-day hourly point forecasts (forecastHourly, forecastGridData) used to compute THI for planned handling days; failure: Show 'no forecast available' and leave the day unclassified. A static portfolio demo must not call it live; use a labelled synthetic forecast file.

provides: State- and region-specific recovery periods, utilization limits, stubble heights and drought phases used as defaults

recommendation: Use as the documented source of configurable defaults (rest periods, use limits, stubble heights), citing the exact document and date.
verification_note: [cite_grazing.json checked[0], claim partly] Fetched with WebFetch; curl gave 'CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403'. Metadata is correct: 'Prescribed Grazing', Range Technical Note No. 9, April 2017, running header 'SOUTH DAKOTA TECHNICAL GUIDE NOTICE SD-424'. VERIFIED: p.4 'Livestock movements should be based on plant growth and utilization and not calendar dates.' and 'Calendar dates may be used as a guide when developing grazing schedules.' p.3 'Keeping the grazing periods as short as practical, especially during periods of fast plant growth, will minimize the opportunity ... to graze plant regrowth prior to plant recovery.' p.3, once-over use ('When two or more pastures are planned to be grazed only one time'): rangeland 'minimum of 45 consecutive days of rest during the growing season', pasture 30. p.3, 2+ grazings ('When two or more pastures are planned to be grazed two or more times during a growing season'): 'Each pasture will be deferred for a minimum of 90 days during the growing season.' The p.4 Table 1 range values match the research: 20-30%* West fast 40, slow 60; East 35/55. 40-50%: West 50/70, East 45/65. Footnote: 'Fast growth usually refers to grasses in a vegetative, pre-boot stage.' Note: 'Under drought conditions, recovery periods may need to be extended to 90 days or longer'. Utilization limits match: 50% seasonal and 30% temporal (p.4), 65% browse and 60% dormant season (p.6). Table 3 (p.6, titled 'Minimum Height of Pasture Species') gives end stubble WWG 4, CWG 3, switchgrass 8, big & sand bluestem 6, KBG 2, sideoats 2, and begin heights WWG 6-10 etc., all as cited. Riparian 'residual heights of 4 to 8 inches is commonly cited as adequate' (Section IV, p.7). App. B p.16: 'Monitor grazing lands frequently and ensure animals have access to dependable water.' Phase I removes 10% in the first month; Phase II removes 20-40% and says 'Routinely monitor conditions such as soil moisture and plant growth on a weekly basis'; Phase III says 'measure remaining forage in all pastures', 'combine remaining herds into one herd', with 30%+ removal on p.16. All verified. MISREAD: the research says '>1 mile to water = very large field needing herding or water relocation'. The source says 'A very large field would roughly be where the distance to water is greater than one mile' ('could be considerably larger on smooth terrain'). Its point is that continuous season-long use gives adequate recovery only on very large fields where livestock are herded or redistributed by changing water. It does not say every field over 1 mile needs herding. The page number for this passage came back inconsistently from two fetches (p.2 and p.3).

name: NDSU Grazing Monitoring Stick protocol (R1780)

recommendation: Recommended manual observation protocol for the phase-3 forage observations.
verification_note: [cite_grazing.json checked[5], claim yes] R1780, Meehan, Sedivec, Printz. 'Revised October 2024'; no original date shown, so the research is correct. Table 1 recovery (min days): rangeland fast (May/June) 45 western ND / 30 eastern; slow (July/August) 65 / 45. Introduced pasture 25/15 fast, 35/25 slow. All match. Measure before turnout and during grazing to prevent overuse; 'Final utilization levels should be evaluated within three days of livestock removal.' 'You should take a minimum of 30 measurements for each key species across a pasture.' Avoid water sources, salt sites and gates. Removal % = (1 - grazed/ungrazed) x 100. WWG: 75% height removal is about 58% by weight (Table 3). Table 5 classes: slight-moderate <40, full 40-60, close 60-80, severe >80. Rule of thumb about 50% by weight. Native cool-season reaches 3.5-leaf mid-late May or early June. One extra point the research did not use: the document also suggests targeting about 50% weight use per grazing period, which is looser than SD TN9's 30% temporal limit. The two sources disagree on the per-stay ceiling.

name: Browser localStorage (Web Storage)
provides: Per-device persistence of small key/value data
access: window.localStorage; synchronous; throws SecurityError when blocked or QuotaExceededError when full
coverage: One browser profile on one device for one origin. http and https are separate stores.
latency: Immediate on this device; never shared.
failure_behavior: Cleared when the last private tab closes. Evicted LRU under storage pressure unless persisted. Safari deletes script-created data after 7 days with no interaction (tracking prevention on). The page must render fully with an empty store.
browser_cors_or_key_issues: Same-origin only; http and https are separate stores. Throws SecurityError when blocked (MDN) and QuotaExceededError when full (WHATWG).
recommendation: Phase 2: per-device conveniences only (selected filter, last review time, an acknowledgement labelled 'this device only'). Never for shared acknowledgements, owners or shelving. The page must render fully with an empty store.
verification_note: [cite_workflow.json checked[23], claim partly] Used in the localStorage integration. SecurityError is confirmed. The page names only SecurityError; it does NOT mention QuotaExceededError or full storage, which comes from WHATWG. The LRU-eviction and Safari 7-day points in failure_behavior come from the MDN quotas page, not this URL.

name: Storage API persistence (navigator.storage.persist)
provides: Asks the browser to exempt the origin from automatic eviction
access: navigator.storage.persist() promise; browser may prompt or decide
failure_behavior: May be denied. The user can still clear data. Does not share data across devices.
browser_cors_or_key_issues: Same device and origin; the browser may prompt or decide.
recommendation: Not needed while localStorage holds only conveniences; it does not share data.
verification_note: [cite_workflow.json checked[24], claim yes] Used in rule 15 and the persist integration. The page reads 'last modified on Jan 5, 2026', which matches. 'In most cases, browsers manage stored data per origin.' It defines best-effort (the default) and persistent storage, and LRU eviction ('The data from the least recently used origin is deleted'). Verbatim: 'Browsers can store up to 5 MiB of local storage, and 5 MiB of session storage per origin' (also 'limited to 10 MiB of data maximum'). Safari: 'If an origin has no user interaction... in the last seven days of browser use, its data created from script will be deleted' when cross-site tracking prevention is on. persist(): Firefox shows a prompt, while Safari and Chromium auto-approve or deny, which supports 'browser may prompt or decide'. When used as the evidence_url for last_review_at, it supports only per-device storage. Calling localStorage 'acceptable' for conveniences is the researcher's judgement.
